title: The unsigned tensor bicomplex and its maps
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and P,Q be N-indexed chain complexes of R-modules [def-weil-pbc-chain-complex-tensor-module]. Define A(P,Q) [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] by A(p,q)=P_p tensor_R Q_q, horizontal differential d_P tensor 1 and vertical differential 1 tensor d_Q. The differentials square to zero and commute. For chain maps a:P→P' and b:Q→Q', define A(a,b) termwise by a_p tensor b_q. Also define chainTensorMap(a,g) for a module map g:N→N' as the chain map P tensor N→P' tensor N' with components a_p tensor g.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right), proof: tensor double complex, cokernel-complex computations and functoriality paragraph; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M3

proof.text: Use Mathlib Functor.mapBifunctorHomologicalComplex with curriedTensor to construct the unsigned bicomplex; tensorBicomplex is only a compatibility abbreviation of its object. Its terms are P_p tensor Q_q, and its two differentials tensor the respective differential with the identity. Define tensorBicomplexMap as a compatibility abbreviation directly of the map of Functor.uncurry.obj applied to this bifunctor, without elaboration-time normalization. The uncurrying map is definitionally the first-variable map followed by the second-variable map, hence its components are a_p tensor b_q. The two cokernel naturality proofs use Mathlib Functor.uncurry_obj_map explicitly to expose this composition before applying the existing component lemmas. Retain mapHomologicalComplex followed by NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex for chainTensorMap. No bespoke bicomplex or morphism data is constructed.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00M3, proof and functoriality paragraph; canonical implementation via Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.Bifunctor and Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Currying
